messages.content: What is the electrostatic potential between two charged bodies of 1e-9 and 2e-9 of distance 0.05?

function.name: calculate_electrostatic_potential
function.description: Calculate the electrostatic potential between two charged bodies using the principle of Coulomb's Law. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge1.description: The quantity of charge on the first body. This is a float type value.

charge2.description: The quantity of charge on the second body. This is a float type value.

distance.description: The distance between the two bodies. This is a float type value.

constant.description: The value of the electrostatic constant. Default is 8.99e9. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Electrostatic interaction energy**

For two point‑like charges \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) separated by a distance \(r\), the electrostatic **potential energy** (the work required to bring them together from infinity) is given by Coulomb’s law:

\[
U \;=\;\frac{k\,q_{1}\,q_{2}}{r}
\]

where  

\(k = 8.988\times10^{9}\,\text{N m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}\).

---

### Plugging in your numbers

| Symbol | Value |
|--------|-------|
| \(q_1\) | \(1\times10^{-9}\,\text{C}\) |
| \(q_2\) | \(2\times10^{-9}\,\text{C}\) |
| \(r\)   | \(0.05\,\text{m}\) |

\[
\begin{aligned}
U &= \frac{(8.988\times10^{9})(1\times10^{-9})(2\times10^{-9})}{0.05}\\[4pt]
&= \frac{(8.988)(2)\times10^{9-9-9}}{0.05}\\[4pt]
&= \frac{17.976\times10^{-9}}{0.05}\\[4pt]
&= 3.5952\times10^{-7}\ \text{J}.
\end{aligned}
\]

So the electrostatic potential energy stored in this configuration is approximately

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle U \approx 3.6\times10^{-7}\ \text{joules}}
\]

---

#### If you were looking for the electric potential at either charge…

- Potential produced by \(q_2\) at the position of \(q_1\):

  \[
  V_{12}= \frac{k\,q_2}{r}= \frac{8.988\times10^{9}(2\times10^{-9})}{0.05}\approx 360~\text{V}
  \]

- Potential produced by \(q_1\) at the position of \(q_2\):

  \[
  V_{21}= \frac{k\,q_1}{r}\approx 180~\text{V}
  \]

But the “interaction” between the two charges—i.e., how much energy it would take to assemble them—is what was calculated above (~\(3.6\times10^{-7}\) J).
